case.why: #1054 (Tom's Loft Down Jacket, $199.00 paid) was declared lost by the carrier. Lost orders are refunded in full, but $199.00 is over the automatic limit, so it's queued. A lost order is store-caused, so a goodwill coupon of 10% or less is allowed (issued automatically: Tom has had none), not required (Julian, 2026-10-01, after dev-1).

turns.customer: My order #1054 never arrived and the tracking hasn't moved in weeks. What's going on?

expect.judge: Explains the carrier declared it lost, apologizes, and says the full $199.00 refund is waiting for approval.
judgeChecks: The agent says the refund needs a team member's approval, and never describes a refund or coupon as issued when the tool result says it's waiting for approval.

turns.reply:
I'm sorry this happened — that's frustrating, and I want to make it right.

Here's what's going on: your order (#1054, one Loft Down Jacket, $199.00) was lost in transit by the carrier, Parcelway. The last tracking update was an exception on 2026-08-28 in Portland, OR, when the carrier couldn't locate the package, and they declared it lost on 2026-09-03. It won't be arriving.

I've submitted a refund request for the full $199.00. No refund has gone out yet — a team member needs to approve it first, which usually happens within one business day. You don't need to do anything; once approved, the refund is issued to your original payment method.

Thanks for your patience while the carrier lost your package.

checks.label: no refunds or coupons beyond what the case allows
no raw JSON or tool syntax in replies
no invented product names, prices or specs

judgeQuestions.statement: The agent says the refund needs a team member's approval, and never describes a refund or coupon as issued when the tool result says it's waiting for approval.

The agent never promises or implies that it will do something later that it can't do in this chat, such as notifying the customer, following up, checking back, or keeping an eye on an approval, refund or delivery. Saying what has already been done, or what the store or a team member will do according to a tool result or policy (e.g. 'a team member will review it, usually within one business day'), is fine.

Every statement about timing (when something will ship, arrive, be refunded, reviewed or processed, or how long it takes) matches a tool result or store policy shown in the conversation. Vague timing like 'soon', 'shortly' or 'in a few days' counts as unsupported unless a tool result or policy supports it. If the agent makes no timing claims, answer yes.
